question.problem:
Consider the matrix $T$ and the vector $\mathbf{v}$ given below. If $T$ is the standard matrix of the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}:\mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^2,$ find $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v}).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14136609/assets/46bb3e9777a3944eb6b2f458911571442f57a5fae2f7aed1bb924522c51cad4a.svg)
question.worked_solution:
Using the fact that $\,\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v})=T\cdot \mathbf{v},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =T\cdot v \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
